programs.title: Truth, integration, and the first playable reference
programs.promise: Agents improve the game that actually runs, not a second implementation or a historical description.
programs.legacy: Existing queue and 47-A/Crucible/Adventure owners; no new dispatcher
programs.baseline: Current root policy, build map, and queue were inspected. PLAN_REGISTRY and FINISH_THE_GAME retain superseded frontend wording; current root policy and ORRERY supersede it. The complete live queue was not executed here.

programs.title: The hand: nimble control without stealing momentum
programs.promise: Every deliberate input produces a trustworthy physical response; earned speed and readable control survive combat.
programs.legacy: PQ-137 / PQ-164 / PQ-189; FUN_CONVERGENCE_LOOP
programs.baseline: The G-mode relative stick is already implemented, with bounded displacement and camera-basis projection. Cruise already filters chip hits. The current Feel Contract contains later speed-normalized B2/B3 amendments: old absolute-radius numbers must not be reinstated.

programs.title: Massline, contact, and terrain as the signature toy
programs.promise: One simple relationship between two bodies produces readable swings, theft, rescue and violent collisions.
programs.baseline: The constraint and physics-authority seams are established. The latest master commit specifically protects kinematic opt-outs; physical affordances must agree with body eligibility.

programs.title: Weapons, states, and combinatorial combat
programs.promise: Every weapon changes a physical situation; shooting remains fun and physical setups expand possibilities rather than replace it.
programs.baseline: Eight bomb payloads and status/field owners already exist; Tarburst is not a new proposal. Bomb target predicates currently omit fauna. New damage/status routes need explicit actor eligibility, not assumed universal support.

programs.title: Readable adversaries and a living encounter director
programs.promise: Enemies reveal intentions the player can disrupt; civilians and specialists share the same physical world.
programs.baseline: The selected AI is SG-06 tactical, not legacy ai.js. The package does not claim current opponents were playtested; behavior weaknesses below are focused questions resolved on ordinary routes.

programs.title: Crucible: the repeatable physics showcase
programs.promise: A run escalates from readable play to spectacular earned chaos, with fast retries and genuinely different builds.
programs.baseline: Crucible wave/arc, survival-style and no-HP-scaling checks exist in package.json. Existing mode owners must be verified at activation; this is not a new survival framework.

programs.title: Adventure: first-hour trust and a complete campaign spine
programs.promise: Personal flight, an owned ship and persistent consequences carry the player from ordinary work into deeper strangeness.
programs.baseline: The repo has a story spine, 47-A and authored physical set pieces. The live mission data declares seventeen types; the module map description saying ten is stale. Do not create another campaign from scratch.

programs.title: Mission craft and authored world-site interactions
programs.promise: Contracts are physical situations with multiple solutions, not interchangeable errands with different nouns.
programs.legacy: PQ-152 / PQ-171 / current world-site kernel; mission briefs M01–M36
programs.baseline: The mission catalog already includes tow_recovery, demolition, rescue_under_fire, authored_set_piece, capital_boss and breakaway_recovery. The human opening raid and Third Shift must be extended or polished, not duplicated.

programs.title: An economy the pilot can understand and physically influence
programs.promise: A contract, trade or theft changes an intelligible local chain of goods, money and opportunity.
programs.legacy: PQ-177 / current economyMissionTerms and custody owners
programs.baseline: The repo already owns supply/demand, mission quotes, cargo, markets and physical trade consequences. This is a coherence and usability expansion, not a replacement economy. All balance values require current route measurement.

programs.title: Mining, salvage and construction as tactile work
programs.promise: Work in the belt is an interesting physical activity, not a progress bar financing the interesting game.
programs.legacy: PQ-145 / PQ-148 / Asteroid Works / current Third Shift owners
programs.baseline: Beam mining, fracture, deep-core drilling, claims and automation already exist. Current Works-screen defects have their own ledger; preserve its ownership and distinguish scheduler symptoms from gameplay changes.

programs.title: Regions, routes and places with a physical identity
programs.promise: Players remember places by how they fly, work and change—not just their skybox color.
programs.legacy: PQ-153 / PQ-154 / world-identity / world-site owners
programs.baseline: The game already has sectors, lanes, authored POIs and an encounter director. Regional proposals below enrich selected existing locations; new region counts are not a release requirement.

programs.title: People, law and memorable consequences
programs.promise: The world understands the difference between a rescue, a mistake and a crime, and gives the pilot something to do about it.
programs.legacy: PQ-149 / PQ-150 / PQ-151 / current recognition and consequence systems
programs.baseline: Reputation, WANTED heat, provenance, returning contacts and consequences are existing owners. The work is to make their causal chain comprehensible and dramatically useful, not add a second reputation axis.

programs.title: Alien ecology that shares the physical world
programs.promise: Animals have motives, anatomy and consequences without becoming a second human combat faction.
programs.legacy: AE-000–349 / PR 170 / existing alien-ecology-program
programs.baseline: PR 170 contains fauna drives, contamination, capture hooks and selected physics bodies. It is unmerged at the audit pin. Capability coverage across ordinary combat/physics tools is not uniform and needs a targeted matrix, not blanket conversion.

programs.title: Xenotechnology: useful matter with strange behavior
programs.promise: Goo, pressure organs and elastic tissue change the fight through honest contact and force—not neon status icons.
programs.legacy: Existing Tarburst/status_goo and Massline owners; XA-051–082 are inspiration, not admitted duplicates
programs.baseline: Tarburst, goo status, mass/inertia response, medium-relative damping and attached residue already exist on master. New matter must add a genuinely different contact or combination law. Earlier chat suggestions about vacuum braking and momentum storage were fantasies, not validated mechanics.

programs.title: Ancient machines that perform consequential work
programs.promise: Verge-Layer machines are surviving institutions whose procedures visibly move, preserve and transform the world.
programs.legacy: AE machine lane / PR 170; deepen existing kinds before adding kinds
programs.baseline: At the pinned PR, machines are spawned collides:false/physicsBody:false and have authored procedure/movement loops. A courier proximity path grants inventory directly; a Mason orbit/beat is not proof of construction. This proposal makes selected workpieces physical without requiring every machine to be a combatant.

programs.title: Precursor geometry as a small coherent force vocabulary
programs.promise: Ancient engineering creates comprehensible spatial rules that can be combined with human tools and biological matter.
programs.legacy: Existing fields and machine-site owners; proposals, not established physics
programs.baseline: Radial/moving fields and machine suppression are already present in different owners. Nonradial/selective effects are proposed extensions; their visual geometry must not claim a force region or conservation law the simulation does not implement.

programs.title: Discovery, behavioral archaeology and bounded regional change
programs.promise: Learning changes the player’s options; physical events change the world; the two must never be conflated.
programs.legacy: AE contamination/revelation / evidence / current sector simulation
programs.baseline: The original brief separates geographic contamination from revelation and asks for lossy shared-memory, progressive strangeness and machine contrast. PR 170 provides initial state/evidence; a full evolving galaxy is neither verified nor necessary.

programs.title: Authored models, spaces and animation at the gameplay camera
programs.promise: Every important object has a strong silhouette, coherent material and visible function in the real game.
programs.legacy: Forge / GRAPHICS_PROGRAM / current release manifests; model briefs A01–A36
programs.baseline: Forge is the established flyable-hull pipeline; PR machine visuals use primitive compositions. That is a source fact, not a live aesthetic verdict. Judge new and existing assets together under current shipping lighting before deciding what must be replaced.

programs.title: Force-readable VFX with materially distinct lifecycles
programs.promise: The player sees where force began, what it acted on, and what continued after the source stopped.
programs.legacy: PQ-134 / PQ-139 / current material VFX owners; effect briefs F01–F32
programs.baseline: The current VFX standard explicitly rejects both generic ball-puffs and thin/frozen wire effects. It calls for substantial evolving material, unequal motion, local contact and persistent cooling. These tasks refine existing owners, not install another VFX engine.

programs.title: Sound, music and silence as mechanical information
programs.promise: Without looking at a meter, the pilot can hear mass, load, danger and release.
programs.legacy: PQ-158 / current audio recipes and voice arbitration; F-series audio requirements
programs.baseline: Audio systems and recipes already exist. Old documents claiming muted or identical sounds are not proof of present defects; audition the current game before replacing anything.

programs.title: ORRERY as a complete usable instrument
programs.promise: The interface makes the game’s choices legible while looking like the same authored instrument everywhere.
programs.legacy: Existing ORRERY redesign lane; minimal feature-required UI writes allowed
programs.baseline: ORRERY is the current direction. Older Field Hardware/approved-image authority is superseded by current root instructions. These outcomes belong to that lane and its component library, not a competing frontend plan.

programs.title: Smoothness, residency and predictable work
programs.promise: Full-quality play remains responsive through cold use, dense action, travel and long sessions.
programs.legacy: Current PERF_BUDGET / VM_LANES / D24–D36 and existing performance owners
programs.baseline: This audit did not measure frame time. Existing logs describe historical latency and resource issues, some already fixed pending validation. First reproduce the current route and attribute the cost; do not copy old perf diagnoses as new facts.

programs.title: Save integrity, input access and product completeness
programs.promise: The game preserves a player’s progress, explains failures, and stays usable across ordinary devices and sessions.
programs.legacy: PQ-164 / PQ-165 / PQ-166 / current save and transition owners
programs.baseline: Browser and Electron share the game route and save contracts. Existing migrations, transition tokens and accessibility support must be extended, not replaced. Language count and platform promises need a scoped launch decision.

programs.title: A finite finish line and the final convergence campaign
programs.promise: One coherent game is finished to a defensible bar; optional ambition remains available without holding it hostage.
programs.legacy: Existing live acceptance matrix and finishing lanes; release preparation remains separately activated
programs.baseline: A-list is a quality aspiration, not a test result or guaranteed commercial outcome. This pack provides coverage, sequencing and proposed evidence. Scope must be fixed to actual retained content; not every optional seed is part of the finish line.

missions.title: The opening raid, made whole
missions.scope: CORE / enrich existing, do not duplicate
missions.types: current opening encounter + current recovery/consequence owners
missions.geometry: Keep the existing hauler lane. Place one useful heavy anchor beside—not across—the escape route, one loose object reachable before the first threat commits, and a clear exit. Size interception distances using actual speeds and time-to-contact, not arbitrary world coordinates.
missions.hook: The fight is already happening during ordinary undock. A short local plea names freight and destination, not a quest menu.
missions.phases: Observe the chase and choose involvement; disrupt one attacker; react to any freight spill or survivor; decide whether to pursue, rescue or leave; return to an existing service for the consequence.
missions.solutions: Protect with ordinary gunfire and cover; use a shove or Massline throw to break pursuit. Do not require both. Missing the pirates may damage freight and change the job.
missions.failure: Convoy damage becomes contested salvage or pilot recovery; the escape route remains open. Failure cannot despawn the on-screen actors just to clear encounter state.
missions.reward: Use current opening rewards. The payoff is one affordable, immediately usable capability or recognition—not a free endgame weapon.
missions.state: Existing encounter completion, stable hauler/cargo IDs, rescue or loss facts, one settlement receipt.
missions.tests: Ignore the event; arrive late; throw an escort into freight; rescue after killing a pirate; save after spill; leave and return. Existing opening is not posted twice.

missions.title: Breakaway freight
missions.types: tow_recovery or an existing authored physical recovery
missions.geometry: A loose cargo train drifts toward a yard obstruction. Provide a broad safe receiving bay and an alternate sling approach. Use a heavy anchor to teach that the pilot moves when the target is too heavy.
missions.hook: A tug requests help with a broken coupler; the cargo is already moving and its manifest is visible.
missions.phases: Identify the valuable segment; match relative velocity; capture it; either tow into the bay or release through the receiving corridor; settle accepted intact quantity.
missions.solutions: Gentle tow using a wide turn; controlled throw with a receiving net. Both use the same physical object and acceptance volume.
missions.failure: Damaged freight pays less and creates a cleanup job; a lost segment is recorded, not magically recreated.
missions.reward: Existing freight reward plus demonstration access to a better coupling tip. No payment for repeatedly crossing the boundary.
missions.state: Workpiece identity, intact/damaged quantity, receiver custody, acceptedOnce.
missions.tests: Save while latched; enter bay backward; oversized hull; full hold; crossing volume twice; cargo cut free beyond camera.

missions.title: Warm cargo, narrow margin
missions.geometry: One volatile crate group moves through a broad lane with optional shorter high-traffic passage. The hazard comes from rough handling and heat, not invisible mines.
missions.hook: A legitimate buyer pays for intact material; the preflight clearly names handling sensitivity and current capacity.
missions.phases: Inspect the load; pick route; handle traffic or a minor disruption; deliver intact units or divert compromised freight to a safe receiver.
missions.solutions: Take the longer cooler lane; use cover and careful propulsion on the shorter path. An emergency jettison is an intentional rescue option.
missions.failure: Partial spoilage reduces payout; dangerous freight can be isolated for salvage. No irreversible campaign blocker.
missions.reward: Net profit after ammunition/repairs is measured; a good run funds a useful early choice.
missions.state: Lot condition and custody, delivery quantity, exposed/isolated state, transaction receipt.
missions.tests: Accept with insufficient space; split a lot; collide at low/high relative speed; abort midrun; save before and after delivery.

missions.title: Counterweight shift
missions.scope: SELECTED / extend Third Shift where overlapping
missions.setting: Current Tethys/SP-07 industrial setting if supported
missions.types: breakaway_recovery or existing Third Shift operations
missions.geometry: A moving industrial component and launcher cadence define a safe interception window. Reuse the actual existing Third Shift geometry; do not mint a new flywheel system.
missions.hook: An existing worker explains the next window and what constitutes a safe handoff.
missions.phases: Observe one full cycle; choose a capture window; couple or redirect the workpiece; carry it clear of the next cycle; return it for a real repair outcome.
missions.solutions: Ride the scheduled motion and release at the tangent; shut down an accessible auxiliary stage and tow slowly at an economic cost.
missions.failure: A missed window creates another attempt or a salvage-recovery branch, not an automatic total loss.
missions.reward: Existing authored reward and restored industrial output, paid once.
missions.state: Current Third Shift workpiece and phase, restored-or-salvaged fact, payment state.
missions.tests: Enter already moving; wait two cycles; save during rotation; premature release; existing story variant already complete.

missions.title: A pod in the crossfire
missions.geometry: A survivor pod lies between two pieces of cover. At least one lateral approach and one sheltered pull line are visible. The pod is sturdy enough for a recovery mistake but not a tank.
missions.hook: A distress cue and identifiable pod appear from a real incident or authored site—not a detached rescue marker.
missions.phases: Locate survivor; choose corridor or suppressor target; attach/reel; transfer custody at a safe berth; meet the saved person later if selected.
missions.solutions: Clear the firing lane then pull; move cover or disable the key attacker and extract while other threats remain.
missions.failure: A damaged pod changes medical/recovery needs. Loss records a consequence; taking no action leaves a comprehensible outcome.
missions.reward: Fair current rescue payment and one future recognition payoff rather than a large universal reputation bonus.
missions.state: Survivor identity, condition, custody and future-recognition eligibility.
missions.tests: Rescuer dies; pod is latched when loading; hostile projectile hits through cover; two receivers; rescue after job timeout.

missions.title: The moving manifest
missions.geometry: A hauler carries a separately readable freight rack, escorted along a route with cover and witnesses. No mandatory pixel-perfect part sniping; an exposed coupler becomes interactable at a readable scale.
missions.hook: A broker identifies a lot, route and legal risk. The player can decline or investigate ownership.
missions.phases: Find the real hauler; observe escort rhythm; separate or recover the flagged lot; break pursuit; choose a lawful return or illicit buyer.
missions.solutions: Disable a coupler and tow the lot without destroying the hauler; go loud and salvage through a more dangerous lawful response.
missions.failure: Destroyed goods cannot satisfy intact theft. A failed theft becomes escape or restitution rather than resetting the lane.
missions.reward: Payout follows actual custody and condition; the illicit route has a distinct market destination.
missions.state: Lot ID and original owner, observed offense, captured/destroyed state, buyer settlement.
missions.tests: Attack wrong hauler; steal then rescue; swap hull; split cargo; re-enter after escape; sell before accepting job.

missions.title: Cargo in the wake
missions.scope: OPTIONAL / combine with an existing heist if similar
missions.geometry: Two ordinary traffic lanes briefly run alongside each other. A transfer window is defined by relative speed and separation, not a pause in the universe.
missions.hook: A client offers a covert physical handoff with an explicit abort option.
missions.phases: Match traffic; approach the marked transfer side; receive or release the lot; avoid inspection or declare; deliver to an existing service.
missions.solutions: Hold a steady formation for a clean transfer; catch a jettisoned package from stand-off with greater detection risk.
missions.failure: A missed handoff leaves a real recoverable package for a bounded time. Detection starts the existing inspection/law process.
missions.reward: Premium for intact covert transfer, ordinary payment for declared delivery where allowed.
missions.state: Transfer token, source/destination custody, reveal state, expiry policy.
missions.tests: Two transfers in one tick; full hold; source leaves sector; tethered package; reload during handoff.

missions.title: The impounded machine
missions.types: authored_set_piece or salvage_retrieval with custody clauses
missions.geometry: A seized workpiece sits in a visible restricted bay with a permitted approach and a physically possible theft route. Security boundaries match the map and signage.
missions.hook: An owner asks for legal release, while a broker offers a faster theft.
missions.phases: Inspect manifest and condition; obtain or recover evidence; choose declaration or covert extraction; handle the resulting custody record.
missions.solutions: Prove rightful ownership via an existing evidence operation; physically steal it and accept the incident and limited buyer options.
missions.failure: Bad evidence is rejected with a reason; theft does not silently clear the original owner. A failed attempt can be abandoned safely.
missions.reward: Returned property produces payment; stolen property produces resale with actual legal costs.
missions.state: Object provenance, evidence reference, impound status, legal-release or theft outcome.
missions.tests: Forged evidence; already-owned object; unrelated cargo in bay; repeated release request; reload after authority changes.

missions.title: The salvage dispute
missions.verbs: inspect, salvage, rescue, negotiate through action
missions.geometry: A valuable wreck and survivor occupy different sides of a field while two claimants arrive on real trajectories. Keep all three objectives visible enough to compare.
missions.hook: A claim beacon identifies a legal conflict; a survivor cue establishes immediate stakes.
missions.phases: Read claim and danger; recover survivor or component; let claimants inspect, or remove contested material; settle the actual chosen outcome.
missions.solutions: Rescue and return evidence to earn lawful recovery; extract the component while containing witnesses/hostility through existing rules.
missions.failure: Delayed salvage may be claimed by another actor, but no invisible despawn or arbitrary murder of a survivor.
missions.reward: Condition-dependent salvage, rescue recognition or restitution obligation; not all simultaneously by default.
missions.state: Wreck claimant, salvaged component ID, survivor state, incident and settlement.
missions.tests: Take component before reading beacon; kill claimant; save with both claims; leave and return.

missions.title: False bloom
missions.setting: Existing clean-side fringe station and claimed contaminated wreck
missions.geometry: A supposedly contaminated workpiece and a known-clean reference sit within safe reach. Sensor disagreement can be tested without entering a lethal zone.
missions.hook: A station restriction rests on an ambiguous report; a worker suspects either fraud or faulty equipment.
missions.phases: Collect baseline reading; change one exposure/stimulus condition; compare with a second instrument; return the supported finding.
missions.solutions: Careful comparison identifies a spoofed signal; physical removal of a suspect transmitter reveals whether the signal follows the object.
missions.failure: Insufficient evidence leaves the restriction in place with a next observation named. Destructive testing may lose compensation, not rewrite truth.
missions.reward: Restored route access or research payment; the player retains evidence after filing.
missions.state: Observation conditions, reference record, tamper fact and accepted report.
missions.tests: Scan repeatedly without intervention; move transmitter; use higher-tier sensor; save between observations; return wrong report.

missions.title: The ship that flew this before
missions.geometry: A fauna route crosses three existing landmarks, ending near a wreck concealed by ordinary geometry. The route is navigable at the player’s real turn radius.
missions.hook: A repeated maneuver resembles a fragment of an old flight recorder.
missions.phases: Observe a complete route; recover the partial recorder; compare two bearings; follow the inferred final leg; physically retrieve one object.
missions.solutions: Use careful observation to follow the animal; use the recorded bearings to take a riskier direct approach after enough evidence.
missions.failure: Losing the creature does not delete the clue. Damaging the recorder reduces certainty and leaves another observation route.
missions.reward: A useful old route or tool location, not an omniscient map reveal.
missions.state: Observed route fragments, recorder condition, inferred discovery and recovered object.
missions.tests: Follow backward; high-speed shortcut; kill creature; reload before comparison; already know destination.

missions.title: Quiet passage
missions.setting: Known route with passive ecology and human traffic
missions.types: passenger_transport or cargo_delivery with declared exposure clause
missions.geometry: A heat-sensitive population creates a safe but slow corridor and a fast exposed bypass. Safe coasting is not enforced with artificial brakes.
missions.hook: A passenger or fragile cargo needs passage without provoking a local population.
missions.phases: Inspect current route knowledge; choose equipment and path; respond to an unexpected heat source; deliver or divert.
missions.solutions: Coast through a known quiet window; deploy an admitted lure and take the quicker lane at material cost.
missions.failure: An alerted animal changes routing rather than instantly killing the passenger; an alternate refuge remains reachable.
missions.reward: A route-use payment plus improved observation confidence; no unlimited per-crossing discovery bonus.
missions.state: Passenger/lot condition, local alert, observed timing and delivery fact.
missions.tests: No lure installed; excessive boost; another ship fires; reload during quiet window; low fuel alternate route.

missions.title: Pay back the wake
missions.setting: Location of a real or authored collateral incident
missions.geometry: The player’s earlier collision left scattered freight along a still-active lane. Preserve actual incident geometry when practical; use a bounded authored fallback for testing.
missions.hook: The damaged party offers a recovery job instead of only a fine.
missions.phases: Inspect obligation; recover the remaining goods or supply replacements; deliver; clear the named portion of the incident.
missions.solutions: Recover original lots carefully; earn money elsewhere and purchase legitimate replacements with a lower-margin outcome.
missions.failure: Further damage increases the particular obligation within declared caps; abandoning preserves the debt without preventing all play.
missions.reward: Incident resolution and restored service/standing, not a farming opportunity.
missions.state: Original incident ID, required/returned quantity, restitution receipt and remaining obligation.
missions.tests: Partial deliveries; duplicate lots; several incidents; reload before settlement; original freight destroyed.

missions.title: A rival remembers
missions.geometry: An escaped rival returns with one visible answer to a witnessed earlier tactic. Preserve terrain options so the counter is not immunity.
missions.hook: A recognizable hull and one short relevant line announce history without a cutscene.
missions.phases: Recognize the changed tool; observe its tell; use an alternate physical approach; defeat, disable or let the rival escape.
missions.solutions: Exploit the countermeasure’s recovery window; use terrain or a different rig rather than out-stat the new defense.
missions.failure: Escape creates a bounded subsequent chapter; repeated return cannot escalate health indefinitely.
missions.reward: Existing bounty or captured fitting, plus a finite rival-history milestone.
missions.state: Observed prior tactic, one admitted adaptation, encounter result and reward eligibility.
missions.tests: Player changed build; no witnessed tactic; rival dies offscreen; save during return; repeated escape cap.

missions.title: Shortage at the gate
missions.setting: Existing trade gate and nearby industrial station
missions.geometry: A closed service lane has one failed mechanical dependency, not a mystery menu lock. An alternate public route prevents trapping the player.
missions.hook: Traffic queues and a specific parts shortage explain the lost service.
missions.phases: Inspect the failed part; source a replacement or salvage it; transport it through a physical obstacle; restore the lane; observe traffic and price response.
missions.solutions: Buy and deliver the correct component; salvage an equivalent workpiece and accept more handling risk.
missions.failure: Bad delivery leaves a recoverable job with partial costs, not a permanently closed mandatory gate.
missions.reward: Payment plus actual route/service restoration and a finite price correction.
missions.state: Failed component, delivered custody, repaired gate/service and one economic event.
missions.tests: Repair before accepting; deliver wrong part; full stock; destroy replacement; reload after reopening.

missions.title: Build your own escape
missions.setting: Existing outlaw transit or arena-derived adventure site
missions.geometry: An escape route lacks a useful anchor but contains a movable heavy wreck. The player may reposition it before taking the dangerous cargo.
missions.hook: A risky pickup gives advance notice of the likely pursuit and leaves preparation time.
missions.phases: Scout route; reposition an anchor or clear cover; take the cargo; choose a sling or gunfight exit; deliver or dump pursuit bait.
missions.solutions: Prepare geometry and escape on a Massline tangent; skip preparation and use conventional cover/fighting with higher pressure.
missions.failure: An anchor lost during setup is not magically replaced; a quieter alternate exit remains possible.
missions.reward: A preparation-sensitive contract payout, no bonus for an exact stunt animation.
missions.state: Prepared object pose, cargo custody, pursuit trigger and escape settlement.
missions.tests: Move anchor too far; fail prep; bring different hull; reload after preparation; enemies displace anchor.

missions.title: The working battlefield
missions.geometry: A functioning conveyor/vent changes available cover on a readable cycle. The machinery is a force source with an observable state, not moving scenery only.
missions.hook: A target facility continues working while its defenders fight.
missions.phases: Observe cycle; choose shutoff or exploitation; break the target with mass or weapons; contain the dangerous aftermath or leave.
missions.solutions: Use the machinery to throw a workpiece through the target; disable the machinery and attack conventionally.
missions.failure: Collateral breaks output and creates a restoration or escape branch, not a reset.
missions.reward: Current demolition reward with condition-sensitive collateral deductions.
missions.state: Machine power/phase, target damage and destruction cause, collateral/repair state.
missions.tests: Destroy source early; target moved; unsafe chain reaction; save while machinery drives a workpiece.

missions.title: The honest shortcut
missions.geometry: A massive legal anchor permits a shorter route, but high exit speed demands an honest braking/runout zone before docking. Current planet rules decide allowed anchors.
missions.hook: A time-sensitive but nonmandatory contract rewards knowledge of local geometry.
missions.phases: Choose route; latch and build speed or take the wide lane; release; brake deliberately; dock safely.
missions.solutions: Execute a clean physical shortcut; take the reliable longer route with less bonus but full base reward.
missions.failure: Missing the time bonus does not fail base delivery. Overshoot costs time, not a hidden teleport back.
missions.reward: Base payment plus bounded punctuality bonus; preserves skill rather than an automatic fast-travel win.
missions.state: Delivery state and optional timing receipt; no per-frame path stored in campaign save.
missions.tests: High-mass hull; no rig; overspeed entry; pause/load; anchor outside allowed capability.

missions.title: Arena of useful wrecks
missions.scope: CORE / Crucible scenario, not campaign mission
missions.geometry: One large anchor, two offset cover masses and a generous escape corridor. Early kills leave useful wrecks whose mass and remaining lifetime are readable.
missions.hook: The first wave teaches the room by letting the player make its next piece of ammunition.
missions.phases: Fight first light threats; use a fresh wreck; react to one counter-tether specialist; earn a breather; draft a physically distinct upgrade.
missions.solutions: Gun-first strategy with terrain defense; rig-first strategy reusing wrecks. Both earn viable progression.
missions.failure: Death explains cause and offers a fast retry with the same seed. The shop never deletes an attached valuable object without defined handoff.
missions.reward: Existing run economy, seed and build identity; no campaign rewards duplicated from a practice run.
missions.state: Current run seed, wave, score, draft and between-wave object policy.
missions.tests: Zero ammunition; no physical kills; wreck pool pressure; wave transition while latched; repeat same seed.

missions.title: A room with a different law
missions.geometry: Reuse a proven arena but change one authored law: a periodic powered conveyor or a moving field source. Do not change every variable or invent a separate combat balance.
missions.hook: A short pre-round demonstration shows the law with an expendable workpiece.
missions.phases: Observe safe demonstration; fight baseline foes; combine the law with a rig; survive one specialist that exploits it; close the round.
missions.solutions: Exploit the field to clear threats; fight in the safe subregion with a positional cost.
missions.failure: A mistake produces a recoverable bad trajectory, not an invisible instant kill.
missions.reward: Run rewards reflect difficulty through positioning and decisions, not higher enemy HP.
missions.state: Arena rule source phase, run state, supported transient cleanup.
missions.tests: Field shutdown; low-mobility build; controller; no rig; dense overlap; reduced-motion cues.

missions.title: Cinder Nursery: the physical return
missions.types: existing ecology mission and world-site operations
missions.geometry: Preserve the existing nursery layout and IDs. Improve the actual power source, relay contact and recovery approach so each action has a visible material consequence.
missions.hook: An ordinary DMC recorder job leads into an infected wreck; vocabulary follows current revelation state.
missions.phases: Arrive quietly; inspect workpiece; restore power; choose whether to sever; unseal with a visible consequence; retrieve recorder; return later.
missions.solutions: Careful low-heat sequence with limited disturbance; intentional severance followed by quicker recovery. Do not script creatures to die when the relay ends.
missions.failure: Bloom changes exposure and routing; a failed first attempt can be recovered without duplicating the recorder.
missions.reward: Existing research/revelation and selected fitting grants, audited for actual fit routes and one-time minting.
missions.state: Existing awake/severed/bloom/objective flags, contamination versus knowledge, dead fauna and grant state.
missions.tests: Sever then bloom; unseal before power if allowed; lose recorder; reload each phase; repeat approach with high knowledge.

missions.title: The sample that must arrive alive
missions.setting: Existing capturable fauna site and research receiver
missions.geometry: A passive specimen lives near a heat source with room for a calm approach. Its cage/socket is large and readable enough for the current camera; no precision tweezer gameplay.
missions.hook: A researcher names one behavior and containment requirement rather than just demanding alien meat.
missions.phases: Identify specimen; lower stress or distract neighbors; capture; choose safe transport route; deliver or release after containment failure.
missions.solutions: Gentle cradle capture; redirect the specimen into a prepared receiving fixture using an admitted lure.
missions.failure: Dead or damaged samples have limited research value but do not satisfy live delivery; safe release is permitted.
missions.reward: One research finding plus condition-sensitive payment; unlock only a capability demonstrated by the result.
missions.state: Fauna stable ID, stress/condition, actor-versus-cargo custody, containment state, delivery receipt.
missions.tests: No quarantine module; full hold; violent capture; release then recapture; save while actor converts to cargo.

missions.title: Glue, meet mass
missions.geometry: One light hostile, one movable wreck and a massive rock provide three mass scales. Keep a clear ordinary gunfight route. The experimental sprayer is given through a real fitting trial, not debug controls.
missions.hook: A prototype field trial asks for an intact capture or material observation, not a mandatory kill trick.
missions.phases: Fit tested prototype; deposit matter; observe coating; attempt an adhesive interaction; recover the workpiece or disable the target; report what happened.
missions.solutions: Bridge light hull to wreck and shove; coat to alter handling, then disable conventionally. Missing the spray does not apply a hidden status.
missions.failure: Broken bridges and lost samples leave known failure observations; no infinite trial ammunition stock outside the bounded job.
missions.reward: Calibration result opens the sterile derivative or a paid prototype choice, not automatic superior DPS.
missions.state: Prototype lease, deposits, attachments, evidence conditions and final settlement.
missions.tests: Exact-body overlap; point-blank fire; high-speed crossing; target dies while bridged; save/reload active residue.

missions.title: Move the nursery, not the animals
missions.setting: Existing carrier/heat-sensitive ecology near a lane
missions.types: escort or authored_set_piece using current ecology offers
missions.geometry: A migrating group is drawn to a heat source crossing commercial traffic. Two lure positions create distinct safe detours; civilian traffic remains physical.
missions.hook: Workers want the lane reopened; researchers want the organisms alive. Both can be satisfied with competent handling, not a forced moral binary.
missions.phases: Read migration and resource attractor; place/transport lure; shepherd across a safe route; manage a predator or impatient hauler; restore normal traffic.
missions.solutions: Move the heat source gradually; use a temporary admitted suppression corridor to guide the group around the hazard.
missions.failure: Injury triggers a bounded panic that changes the route; recovery or partial success remains possible.
missions.reward: Lane-service payment and ecological observation; killing everything is an inferior but explicitly accounted fallback where allowed.
missions.state: Group destination, lure lifetime, carrier condition, lane state and one resolution.
missions.tests: Lure destroyed; player leaves; kill relay; unrelated ship fires; save during migration; no suitable equipment.

missions.title: A fossil made of motion
missions.setting: Existing route-memory site, not a new full region
missions.geometry: Two hosts from different local strains react to one archived signal near recognizable landmarks. The route destination is optional and recovery-safe.
missions.hook: An old recording triggers an oddly familiar motion in an otherwise simple creature.
missions.phases: Observe baseline; play the controlled signal through an existing site emitter; compare strain reactions; follow the repeated fragment; file limited evidence.
missions.solutions: Use a portable admitted recorder at safe range; restore the site emitter and accept that more local fauna may react.
missions.failure: No response is a valid finding if the conditions were correct. Aggression interrupts but does not fabricate evidence.
missions.reward: A useful timing/route clue and a narrowly defined research unlock; the origin remains uncertain.
missions.state: Stimulus identity, sampled hosts, observed reactions and inference confidence.
missions.tests: Wrong recording; same host twice; relay off; player fires during test; load mid-observation.

missions.title: The station that kept breathing
missions.geometry: A station valve cycle drives a visible pressure/flow effect and nourishes attached biology. Model only the exterior and accessible workpieces; no new walkable-interior game.
missions.hook: A maintenance signal continues despite the station being abandoned.
missions.phases: Observe valve timing; trace biological dependence; isolate one branch or vent safely; recover a service recorder/workpiece; decide whether to leave the cycle running.
missions.solutions: Synchronize recovery with the existing cycle; shut down the heat/valve branch and accept ecological consequences.
missions.failure: Rupture alters local exposure and routes but leaves an escape; the station cannot become an invulnerable cutscene object.
missions.reward: Industrial salvage and one causal finding about infrastructure occupation.
missions.state: Valve/power state, isolated branch, recovered item, local biomass/activity facts.
missions.tests: Break power early; force open wrong valve; return after shutdown; save while pressure builds.

missions.title: Dead-letter delivery
missions.setting: Existing Listening Field and recipient machine site
missions.types: salvage_retrieval or authored_set_piece with machine procedure
missions.geometry: A Courier carries one visible token between two known local endpoints. A safe interception leg and a recipient holding volume are readable at normal speed.
missions.hook: A machine repeats a failed delivery cycle. An interpreted directive asks for RETURN only after the player earns enough understanding.
missions.phases: Follow the Courier; discover why the recipient refuses; physically recover the token; repair or satisfy the recipient condition; deliver it and watch downstream work resume.
missions.solutions: Escort the Courier through an obstruction; take custody of the token and complete the route yourself.
missions.failure: Delay stalls the operation but does not destroy the campaign. Lost token has a declared recovery/remint policy with duplicate protection.
missions.reward: A narrow machine permission and a restored work cycle, not a universal robot reputation boost.
missions.state: Token ID, sender/holder/recipient custody, acknowledged delivery, downstream work order.
missions.tests: Catch before offered; return to wrong recipient; leave sector carrying token; reload while receiver accepts; token destroyed.

missions.title: A place for the missing piece
missions.geometry: A missing structural insert and its receiving socket share a clear outline. A powered machine field helps alignment but does not teleport the piece.
missions.hook: A Custodian repeats a stalled repair. Its work light points to the absent part.
missions.phases: Identify matching component; tow it within work reach; align or activate the field; hold clear while the robot performs actual repair; observe restored function.
missions.solutions: Use the Massline to orient and deliver; power the safe alignment field and guide the piece through it.
missions.failure: Bad alignment is refused clearly; a damaged substitute can work with reduced output or further repair.
missions.reward: Reopened service/corridor and a documented equipment permission, granted once.
missions.state: Part custody and condition, repair progress, site restoration and credential state.
missions.tests: Wrong piece; forced impact; move during welding; save at partial repair; machine source removed.

missions.title: Two correct orders
missions.setting: Existing boundary between two machine work volumes
missions.geometry: One workpiece lies between preservation and reclamation volumes. Each machine stops at its own finite jurisdiction; neither blindly fights through the other.
missions.hook: Two exact directives refer to the same object with incompatible classifications.
missions.phases: Observe both procedures; gather the specific current condition evidence; move or isolate the workpiece; present the finding; receive a bounded decision.
missions.solutions: Prove contamination changed the object’s class; relocate it into a permitted preservation volume with an economic or route cost.
missions.failure: Inconclusive evidence leaves a safe stalemate and optional return; no permanent tug-of-war consumes the sector CPU.
missions.reward: One permitted route or preserved research object; the creators’ intent remains unknown.
missions.state: Workpiece classification, local evidence, jurisdiction ownership and procedure terminal state.
missions.tests: Object exactly on boundary; rapid crossings; irrelevant evidence; reload both machines waiting; player destroys workpiece.

missions.title: The clean cylinder
missions.setting: Existing Shepherd corridor through high contamination
missions.geometry: A moving suppression pocket provides a finite safe route; clear entry/exit refuge makes its timing learnable. Suppression changes coordination, not biomass or inertia by fiat.
missions.hook: A convoy requests escort through a known machine-maintained corridor.
missions.phases: Join the moving pocket; escort traffic; respond to one machine fault or drifting obstruction; restore movement or divert to refuge; complete passage.
missions.solutions: Keep the Shepherd functional and match pace; take a prepared longer boundary route using lures or quiet travel.
missions.failure: A failing pocket gives a telegraphed retreat window. No invisible mass death the moment the field ends.
missions.reward: Convoy payment and stronger local route knowledge; no complete immunity technology.
missions.state: Convoy progress, Shepherd operation, suppression source state and refuge/arrival outcome.
missions.tests: Machine stopped; excessive player speed; convoy split; carrier enters; save in pocket; leave to obtain repair part.

missions.title: The Mason moves the cover
missions.setting: Existing machine construction site under human attack
missions.geometry: The cover asteroid is a real scheduled workpiece. The Mason moves it slowly enough to read but enough to change firing lanes. A safe alternate cover remains.
missions.hook: A human fight happens inside an ancient maintenance operation that will not politely pause for it.
missions.phases: Enter fight; notice workpiece motion; choose whether to protect, interrupt or exploit it; resolve the human objective; witness completed relocation.
missions.solutions: Use the moving mass as cover/ammunition at a controlled cost; isolate the local drive source and fight conventionally.
missions.failure: Interrupting construction records an unresolved machine obligation; it does not instantly revoke every route.
missions.reward: Human objective reward plus an optional restoration consequence.
missions.state: Work order, workpiece pose, human objective and local interruption fact.
missions.tests: Workpiece hit by bombs; tethered by player; target dies under moving rock; save midmove; field turns off.

missions.title: Two ships, one mistake
missions.geometry: An alien adhesive incident bridges two medium bodies on diverging trajectories. Multiple accessible endpoints allow cutting, towing or counter-impulse; no permanent player control lock.
missions.hook: A prototype shipment leaked during a collision. One crew wants separation, the other wants the valuable cargo preserved.
missions.phases: Assess bridge tension; reduce relative speed; choose a severing or stabilizing method; remove residue or tow the pair to service; settle damage honestly.
missions.solutions: Purge/cut the bridge at low load; synchronize both bodies and carry them as a pair with deliberate mass costs.
missions.failure: A violent snap scatters recoverable cargo and creates rescue pressure instead of a scripted explosion.
missions.reward: Condition-sensitive recovery pay and material evidence; no bonus for harming civilians deliberately.
missions.state: Bridge endpoints/load, custody and damage, separated/paired delivery, one settlement.
missions.tests: Endpoint destroyed; zero separation; extra field applied; reload under load; player leaves neighborhood.

missions.title: At the edge of order
missions.geometry: A selected physical containment plane—not mere coherence field—separates two combat spaces. Its finite edge permits flanking. Ordinary hulls and one admitted material category have explicit distinct behavior.
missions.hook: A human convoy crosses while reactive alien matter reaches the boundary.
missions.phases: Observe the material selectivity; protect the crossing; exploit or clear the accumulated matter; exit before a declared power interruption.
missions.solutions: Use the plane to block adhesive ordnance while escorting; take the edge route and fight without relying on the field.
missions.failure: Power loss releases the constraint only as its real law specifies; no magical stored explosion unless explicitly modeled.
missions.reward: Escort payment and a precise observation of the field, not universal permission control.
missions.state: Field source and selectivity class, convoy state, accumulated gameplay parcels and transient cleanup.
missions.tests: Edge crossing; plane off; high-speed projectile; material count cap; bloom/reducedflash; save transition.

missions.title: The harvest somebody else owns
missions.setting: Existing wreck field near a Sorter
missions.geometry: A Sorter visibly approaches a finite set of unprotected debris after a battle. The valuable workpiece has enough warning time for a normal pilot to act.
missions.hook: A lawful salvage claim meets ancient maintenance rules.
missions.phases: Identify the desired component; decide quick extraction or permitted preservation; intercept its transport if needed; deliver or present classification evidence.
missions.solutions: Recover before processing; change its classification through a real custody/preservation action that the machine recognizes.
missions.failure: Processed material becomes a lesser recoverable resource, not a silently deleted prize. Essential story objects are excluded.
missions.reward: Original salvage value or lower processed value; machine permission is local and specific.
missions.state: Salvage object ID, sorter work order/custody, processed resource and settlement.
missions.tests: Kill occurs offscreen; protected wreck; partial extraction; reload before processing; player towing another object.

missions.title: The route that closes ahead
missions.scope: OPTIONAL LATE CAMPAIGN / no required new ending
missions.setting: Existing deep approach and gate network
missions.geometry: A finite sequence of local closures threatens a convoy route. Every state retains a reachable refuge or remedy, and map updates reflect observed—not omniscient—knowledge.
missions.hook: Ancient machines begin a containment sequence for a physical reason the player can partly observe.
missions.phases: Identify first closure; compare signals and route records; choose a refuge or a specific appeal/repair; move the mission object; witness the consequence without an apex reveal.
missions.solutions: Repair or satisfy one limited transit condition; take a known longer null corridor at a resource cost.
missions.failure: Missed timing changes destination or rescue requirements, never permanently traps a low-resource save.
missions.reward: Campaign progression through an established arc plus bounded route knowledge; Vethari remain indirect.
missions.state: Closure sequence, known graph, refuge reachable predicate, current story facts and completed obligation.
missions.tests: Low fuel; wrong credential; player already behind closure; save at every transition; ignored optional clues.

missions.title: The universe keeps working
missions.scope: CORE FINISH ROUTE / composite acceptance, not a new mission
missions.setting: Chosen ordinary region + one finished alien and machine site
missions.types: existing modes, missions and story chain
missions.verbs: fly, work, fight, fit, discover, return
missions.geometry: Use actual retained locations and travel links. No special acceptance-only world, cheat inventory or reduced detail.
missions.hook: A fresh save begins with the ordinary game and can reach the selected frontier through legitimate progression.
missions.phases: Boot; play first fight; complete a job; trade and fit; fail and recover; visit an alien site; interact with a machine; save, reload and return to see consequences.
missions.solutions: Combat-focused and work/exploration-focused progression both reach the selected frontier without identical grinding.
missions.failure: Ordinary mistakes create supported recovery; actual corruption, softlock or missing asset is a blocker to fix.
missions.reward: The reward is verified product confidence, not an in-game completion bonus.
missions.state: Existing world/save/run state only; no new acceptance progression.
missions.tests: Fresh controls; alternate devices; varied viewport; browser/Electron; legitimate low resources; long session; save interrupted safely.
